# Data Inventory

All raw files: `challange information document/BMW-Data/` (read-only, git-ignored). Profiled 2026-10-10; re-verified 2026-10-10 (pandas 3 in a `uv` Python 3.12 env + openpyxl/pdftotext).

**Counting rule:** the feedback files have one row per (verbatim × classification). All verbatim counts below are **unique `ID`s** unless a column says "rows".

## 1. Customer feedback (verbatims) — `{F70,G60,G70}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`

Sheet `Feedback_Explorer`, 12 columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Verbatim ID, e.g. `G60-0001`. **Not unique per row** — one row per (verbatim × classification). An ID never spans two sources. |
| `Source` | Anonymized channel `Source A`–`D` (interpretation open, Q-005) |
| `Brand`, `Sales Description` | `[BMW]`, `[BMW 5 Series]` |
| `Country` | ISO-2 (US, GB, JP, KR, …) |
| `Derivate (e-code)` | F70 / G60 / G70 |
| `Engine Type` | `ICE`, `PHEV`, `BEVE` (= BEV; the raw value is `BEVE`) |
| `Feedback Type` | `Likes`, `Difficult to Use`, `Defect`, `Wants`, or empty (unclassified) |
| `Customer Feedback` | Free text, mean ~215–225 chars per verbatim (Source D ~125) |
| `Vfc level2 3 Name` | Combined "Component : Issue" label |
| `Vfc level2 Name` | Component / topic (e.g. `Seats`, `Touch screen, operation`, `Electric Range`) |
| `Vfc level3 Name` | Issue type (e.g. `Not user-friendly`, `Like: function`, `Customer request: function`) |

| File | Rows | Verbatims (unique IDs) | Sources (verbatims) | Countries (verbatims) | Engines (verbatims) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 4,076 | 2,128 | A 2,128 | GB 1,293, **JP 672**, SE 71, FR 53, AU 16, FI 8, DK 8, KR 4 | ICE 2,128 |
| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 | B 2,626, A 854, C 384, D 136 | **US 3,610 (90%)**, KR 205, JP 53, GB 36, SE 28, DK 20, CA 18, … | ICE 2,259, BEV 1,363, PHEV 378 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 | B 2,853, A 695, C 314, D 138 | **US 3,792 (95%)**, KR 137, JP 40, CA 8, GB 8, … | ICE 2,568, BEV 1,129, PHEV 303 |

European verbatims: F70 ~1,430 (67%), G60 ~110, **G70 ~19**. Row counts overstate Source A, which carries the most multi-label rows: G60 Source A has 1,858 rows but only 854 verbatims.

Quirks:
- **Dedupe by `ID`** when counting verbatims; keep all rows as classification labels.
- **Unclassified verbatims:**
  - Source A: `Feedback Type` empty ⇔ `Vfc level2 = no_class_found`. That is 300 of F70's 2,128 verbatims (14%; 27% of rows).
  - Source D: no BMW classification at all.
  - Source C: ~70 verbatims per file have an empty type *and* an empty topic.
  - → Our own LLM classification is needed; the BMW taxonomy is a hint.
- 120 (F70) / 221 (G60) / 211 (G70) distinct `Vfc level2` values incl. `no_class_found`. Top topics: Drivetrain, Handling/Riding, Body equipment, Exterior design, Seats, Touch screen, Electric Range.
- Observed text patterns per source. These are **observations, not channel identities** (Q-005):
  - **A:** all derivatives, many countries (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized text ("the car…", "i really…"), so possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only; most verbatims start "Customer stated / mentioned / reported / commented…" (third-person notes).
  - **C:** US only; ~30–40% start "I had a minor/serious problem with…", others "What is…" / "If there…" (structured survey prompts); mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short; unclassified. Two prompt templates in G60 (checked 2026-10-10): 34 of 136 end with "That is the one thing could be most improved about the <area> of my vehicle" (improvement answers, e.g. "the head rests are too short"); the rest are mostly "love the…" answers. So D mixes "what do you like" and "what could be most improved" — the earlier note that D is **not** improvement feedback was wrong.
- **No China verbatims** for any derivative. There is **no date column** — no time series possible.

## 2. Customer studies — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`

### Sheet `CN_EU_2025` (76 content rows; openpyxl reports 84 incl. trailing empty rows)
- Columns: China → `BMW 5 Series G68`, `BMW 7 Series G70`; EU → `BMW 1 Series F70`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 37 categories, each a label row followed by a `Mean` row. Values are **numeric cells** (format `#,##0.00`), range ~6.5–9.9. Scale unconfirmed (0–10 or 1–10?; Q-006).
- **No sample sizes.**
- Categories: overall satisfaction, exterior/interior styling, interior quality, equipment level, safety, squeaks/rattles, value for money, reliability, visibility, controls/displays, smartphone integration, infotainment features + ease of use, navigation, seating comfort, small-item storage, acceleration, roadholding, efficiency, braking, sportiness, prestige, manoeuvrability, ride quality, front/rear roominess, luggage loading + capacity, ingress/egress, environmental friendliness, HVAC, build quality, quietness, driving position, connected services, interior versatility.

### Sheet `US_2025` (929 content rows; openpyxl reports 934)
- Columns: question, `% of column, sample base`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 103 questions, each block = `Sample total` + 7-point distribution: I Hate It / A Failure / Unsatisfactory / Satisfactory / Excellent / Delightful / I Love It. Shares 0–1; every block sums to 1.0.
- **`Sample total` = 1 is the share base, not a respondent count → no sample sizes.** No significance testing or n-weighting is possible.
- Granular: exterior (proportions, wheels, door handles, lights, door sound), driving (ride, handling, power), interior (materials, seats per row, roominess, storage, cupholders, cargo), climate, audio, controls intuitiveness, NVH, …
- **No F70 in US.**
- Useful derived metrics: top-2-box (Delightful + I Love It), bottom-3-box, net score. CN/EU means and US distributions are **not directly comparable** (Q-006).

## 3. Sales volumes — `sales_volumes.xlsx`

Sheets `F70`, `G60_G68`, `G70`; columns `market, market_code, volume_2024, volume_2025, volume_2030` (2030 = forecast).

| Derivative | EU 25 | CN 25 | US 25 | RoW 25 | Total 24 → 25 → 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 85k | 0 | 0 | 28k | 105k → 113k → 118k |
| G60/G68 | 115k | 75k | 78k | 28k | 278.6k → 296k → 316k |
| G70 | 13k | 10k | 12k | 7k | 34k → 42k → 52k |

- The F70 sheet's China 2024 cell (C3) is a **formula** (`=-D3-C10`) with cached value 0, not a typed number (found at ingest 2026-10-10; stored as 0, formula kept in metadata).
- **No powertrain split**, although `data_and_source.png` says "units by powertrain and region". Engine mix can only be inferred from feedback.
- `G60_G68` is one combined sheet, with no G60/G68 split. CN is presumably the G68 LWB.
- **Values look stylized and conflict with public data** (Q-015):
  - All values except one are round thousands.
  - G60/G68 CN is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025. Public figures point the other way: 5 Series China (China-built) Jan–Nov 2025 was 107,348 per CPCA via Gasgoo, and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5% in 2025 (`competitor-landscape.md`, `portfolio-reference.md`).
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce; "Europe" definitions differ).
  - Until clarified, treat the file as **BMW-internal relative weights**, and surface the conflict instead of mixing both sources.

## 4. Equipment / option lists — `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF`

- German-market price lists, **in German**, text-extractable (`pdftotext -layout` works):

  | File | PDF title | Edition | Pages |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | F70 | "BMW 1er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 23 |
  | G60 | "BMW 5er **Limousine** Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 2, 22.06.2026 | 28 |
  | G70 | "BMW 7er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 27 |

  The G60 list covers the sedan incl. i5 — **no Touring (G61)**.
- Sections: Fahrzeugpreise (models, power, consumption, price), Serienausstattung(en) (standard equipment per model), M Sportpaket / Pro, Räder & Reifen, Farbwelt, **Sonderausstattungen (options)**, Technische Werte.
- Matrix tables use `■` = standard; options with price.
- Use: baseline "what the car offers today", package structure, gaps vs. competitors.
- The briefing promises equipment "by trim and **market**", but only DE was provided. For US/CN it's an **assumption** that equipment is comparable.

## 5. Briefing material
- `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (2 pages). **Image-only (no text layer):** `pdftotext` returns nothing, so render it (`pdftoppm`) to read it.
- `mission.md`.
- `data_and_source.png`: dataset purpose table.
- `image_1.png`: "1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car" + example verbatims/themes.
- `image_2.png`: reference process.

## Coverage matrix (what we can say where)

| | EU | US | CN | RoW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | ~1.4k verbatims (GB-heavy), study, sales | — | — | **~690 verbatims (JP 672)**, sales |
| G60/G68 | ~110 verbatims, study, sales | **~3.6k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study (G68), sales | ~280 verbatims (KR 205, JP, CA), sales |
| G70 | ~19 verbatims (≈ none), study, sales | **~3.8k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study, sales | ~190 verbatims (KR 137, JP), sales |

- RoW verbatims (JP/KR/CA/AU) are separate customer groups under D-011 — don't fold them into EU.
- External/web data fills gaps: competitors (Mercedes E/S/A-Class, Audi A6/e-tron, Tesla, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto, BYD…), reviews, trends.

| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 | B 2,626, A 854, C 384, D 136 | **US 3,610 (90%)**, KR 205, JP 53, GB 36, SE 28, DK 20, CA 18, … | ICE 2,259, BEV 1,363, PHEV 378 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 | B 2,853, A 695, C 314, D 138 | **US 3,792 (95%)**, KR 137, JP 40, CA 8, GB 8, … | ICE 2,568, BEV 1,129, PHEV 303 |

European verbatims: F70 ~1,430 (67%), G60 ~110, **G70 ~19**. Row counts overstate Source A, which carries the most multi-label rows: G60 Source A has 1,858 rows but only 854 verbatims.

Quirks:
- **Dedupe by `ID`** when counting verbatims; keep all rows as classification labels.
- **Unclassified verbatims:**
  - Source A: `Feedback Type` empty ⇔ `Vfc level2 = no_class_found`. That is 300 of F70's 2,128 verbatims (14%; 27% of rows).
  - Source D: no BMW classification at all.
  - Source C: ~70 verbatims per file have an empty type *and* an empty topic.
  - → Our own LLM classification is needed; the BMW taxonomy is a hint.
- 120 (F70) / 221 (G60) / 211 (G70) distinct `Vfc level2` values incl. `no_class_found`. Top topics: Drivetrain, Handling/Riding, Body equipment, Exterior design, Seats, Touch screen, Electric Range.
- Observed text patterns per source. These are **observations, not channel identities** (Q-005):
  - **A:** all derivatives, many countries (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized text ("the car…", "i really…"), so possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only; most verbatims start "Customer stated / mentioned / reported / commented…" (third-person notes).
  - **C:** US only; ~30–40% start "I had a minor/serious problem with…", others "What is…" / "If there…" (structured survey prompts); mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short; unclassified. Two prompt templates in G60 (checked 2026-10-10): 34 of 136 end with "That is the one thing could be most improved about the <area> of my vehicle" (improvement answers, e.g. "the head rests are too short"); the rest are mostly "love the…" answers. So D mixes "what do you like" and "what could be most improved" — the earlier note that D is **not** improvement feedback was wrong.
- **No China verbatims** for any derivative. There is **no date column** — no time series possible.

## 2. Customer studies — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`

### Sheet `CN_EU_2025` (76 content rows; openpyxl reports 84 incl. trailing empty rows)
- Columns: China → `BMW 5 Series G68`, `BMW 7 Series G70`; EU → `BMW 1 Series F70`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 37 categories, each a label row followed by a `Mean` row. Values are **numeric cells** (format `#,##0.00`), range ~6.5–9.9. Scale unconfirmed (0–10 or 1–10?; Q-006).
- **No sample sizes.**
- Categories: overall satisfaction, exterior/interior styling, interior quality, equipment level, safety, squeaks/rattles, value for money, reliability, visibility, controls/displays, smartphone integration, infotainment features + ease of use, navigation, seating comfort, small-item storage, acceleration, roadholding, efficiency, braking, sportiness, prestige, manoeuvrability, ride quality, front/rear roominess, luggage loading + capacity, ingress/egress, environmental friendliness, HVAC, build quality, quietness, driving position, connected services, interior versatility.

### Sheet `US_2025` (929 content rows; openpyxl reports 934)
- Columns: question, `% of column, sample base`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 103 questions, each block = `Sample total` + 7-point distribution: I Hate It / A Failure / Unsatisfactory / Satisfactory / Excellent / Delightful / I Love It. Shares 0–1; every block sums to 1.0.
- **`Sample total` = 1 is the share base, not a respondent count → no sample sizes.** No significance testing or n-weighting is possible.
- Granular: exterior (proportions, wheels, door handles, lights, door sound), driving (ride, handling, power), interior (materials, seats per row, roominess, storage, cupholders, cargo), climate, audio, controls intuitiveness, NVH, …
- **No F70 in US.**
- Useful derived metrics: top-2-box (Delightful + I Love It), bottom-3-box, net score. CN/EU means and US distributions are **not directly comparable** (Q-006).

## 3. Sales volumes — `sales_volumes.xlsx`

Sheets `F70`, `G60_G68`, `G70`; columns `market, market_code, volume_2024, volume_2025, volume_2030` (2030 = forecast).

| Derivative | EU 25 | CN 25 | US 25 | RoW 25 | Total 24 → 25 → 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 85k | 0 | 0 | 28k | 105k → 113k → 118k |
| G60/G68 | 115k | 75k | 78k | 28k | 278.6k → 296k → 316k |
| G70 | 13k | 10k | 12k | 7k | 34k → 42k → 52k |

- The F70 sheet's China 2024 cell (C3) is a **formula** (`=-D3-C10`) with cached value 0, not a typed number (found at ingest 2026-10-10; stored as 0, formula kept in metadata).
- **No powertrain split**, although `data_and_source.png` says "units by powertrain and region". Engine mix can only be inferred from feedback.
- `G60_G68` is one combined sheet, with no G60/G68 split. CN is presumably the G68 LWB.
- **Values look stylized and conflict with public data** (Q-015):
  - All values except one are round thousands.
  - G60/G68 CN is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025. Public figures point the other way: 5 Series China (China-built) Jan–Nov 2025 was 107,348 per CPCA via Gasgoo, and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5% in 2025 (`competitor-landscape.md`, `portfolio-reference.md`).
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce; "Europe" definitions differ).
  - Until clarified, treat the file as **BMW-internal relative weights**, and surface the conflict instead of mixing both sources.

## 4. Equipment / option lists — `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF`

- German-market price lists, **in German**, text-extractable (`pdftotext -layout` works):

  | File | PDF title | Edition | Pages |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | F70 | "BMW 1er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 23 |
  | G60 | "BMW 5er **Limousine** Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 2, 22.06.2026 | 28 |
  | G70 | "BMW 7er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 27 |

  The G60 list covers the sedan incl. i5 — **no Touring (G61)**.
- Sections: Fahrzeugpreise (models, power, consumption, price), Serienausstattung(en) (standard equipment per model), M Sportpaket / Pro, Räder & Reifen, Farbwelt, **Sonderausstattungen (options)**, Technische Werte.
- Matrix tables use `■` = standard; options with price.
- Use: baseline "what the car offers today", package structure, gaps vs. competitors.
- The briefing promises equipment "by trim and **market**", but only DE was provided. For US/CN it's an **assumption** that equipment is comparable.

## 5. Briefing material
- `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (2 pages). **Image-only (no text layer):** `pdftotext` returns nothing, so render it (`pdftoppm`) to read it.
- `mission.md`.
- `data_and_source.png`: dataset purpose table.
- `image_1.png`: "1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car" + example verbatims/themes.
- `image_2.png`: reference process.

## Coverage matrix (what we can say where)

| | EU | US | CN | RoW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | ~1.4k verbatims (GB-heavy), study, sales | — | — | **~690 verbatims (JP 672)**, sales |
| G60/G68 | ~110 verbatims, study, sales | **~3.6k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study (G68), sales | ~280 verbatims (KR 205, JP, CA), sales |
| G70 | ~19 verbatims (≈ none), study, sales | **~3.8k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study, sales | ~190 verbatims (KR 137, JP), sales |

- RoW verbatims (JP/KR/CA/AU) are separate customer groups under D-011 — don't fold them into EU.
- External/web data fills gaps: competitors (Mercedes E/S/A-Class, Audi A6/e-tron, Tesla, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto, BYD…), reviews, trends.

content.content:
# BMW Group Report 2025 — extract for the knowledge base

**Source:** BMW Group Report 2025 (published Mar 2026, PDF created 2 Mar 2026, 434 pages), https://www.bmwgroup.com/content/dam/grpw/websites/bmwgroup_com/ir/downloads/en/2026/bericht/BMW-Group-Report-2025-en.pdf. Retrieved 2026-10-10.
**Trust tier:** T1 (official OEM annual report, audited parts by PwC). **Page numbers** = printed page = PDF page.
**Why:** BMW support (2026-10-10) recommended the report for (1) market & sales data and (2) product strategy & R&D. Only these two areas are extracted; the financial statements are skipped.

**How to use:**
- **Evidence:** these are evidence for *market context and BMW's strategic direction*.
- **Not feasibility:** they are **not** engineering feasibility proof, and they don't turn engineering topics into customer requirements (scope: `challenge-brief.md` → Scope tensions, Q-010).
- **Rounding:** figures are as printed; the report rounds per commercial practice (p. 7).
- **Supersedes:** this final report supersedes the provisional January 2026 press-release figures (`portfolio-reference.md` §3).

---

## 1. Market & sales data

### 1.1 Deliveries 2025 (final)

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 | Δ | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BMW Group (Automotive) deliveries | 2,450,854 | **2,463,681** | +0.5% | 9, 12, 77 |
| BMW brand | 2,200,217 | 2,169,739 | −1.4% | 12, 77 |
| MINI | 244,925 | 288,278 | +17.7% | 12, 80 |
| Rolls-Royce | 5,712 | 5,664 | −0.8% | 12, 80 |
| BMW M GmbH | 206,587 | 213,449 | +3.3% | 79 |

- **Final vs. provisional:** the January press release had 2,463,715 / 2,169,761 (provisional). The report's figures are final, so the "typo" assumption in `portfolio-reference.md` §5 was wrong.
- **BMW brand without China:** sales grew **+4.2%** (p. 78).
- **BMW brand in China:** monthly deliveries were "roughly 50,000 units" at year-end (p. 78).

### 1.2 Regional trends (BMW Group incl. Rolls-Royce, in 1,000 units, p. 78)

| Region | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | **2025** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Europe | 949.1 | 878.5 | 943.0 | 948.5 | **1,017.6** |
| – Germany | 266.8 | 254.3 | 272.6 | 265.7 | 288.5 |
| – UK | 164.3 | 157.3 | 159.2 | 168.8 | 171.4 |
| Americas | 451.7 | 441.5 | 482.0 | 482.7 | **509.9** |
| – USA | 368.0 | 363.5 | 397.3 | 399.3 | **419.2** |
| Asia | 1,067.9 | 1,031.0 | 1,073.1 | 963.6 | **874.1** |
| – China | 847.9 | 793.5 | 826.3 | 715.2 | **626.0** |
| Other markets | 52.8 | 48.6 | 56.1 | 56.1 | 62.1 |
| Total | 2,521.5 | 2,399.6 | 2,554.2 | 2,450.9 | 2,463.7 |

- **Growth by region:** Europe +7.3%, Americas +5.6%, China −12.5% (p. 77). China declined in both 2024 and 2025 (826.3k → 715.2k → 626.0k).
- **BMW brand, share of sales by market** (2025, with 2024 in brackets; p. 78):

  | Market | 2025 (2024) |
  |---|---|
  | China | **25.4% (29.2%)** |
  | USA | 17.0% (16.3%) |
  | Germany | 11.7% (10.8%) |
  | UK | 7.0% (6.9%) |
  | Italy | 3.6% |
  | France | 3.5% |
  | South Korea | 3.5% |
  | Other | 28.3% |

- **Total market growth 2025** (all vehicle groups served by BMW; p. 67):

  | Market | Change |
  |---|---|
  | Europe | +2.2% (DE +1.4, FR −5.1, IT −2.5, ES +13.1, UK +3.5) |
  | USA | +2.4% |
  | China | +3.2% |
  | Japan | +3.3% |
  | South Korea | +4.8% |
  | World | +3.3% (82.3 M) |

  - **China market vs. BMW:** the market grew while BMW fell 12.5%.
  - **China's growth segment:** growth was "dominated by vehicles priced at 150,000 renminbi or less" and the "trend toward local manufacturers continued" (p. 67).

### 1.3 Deliveries by model series (BMW brand, p. 79)

| Model series | 2024 | 2025 | Δ | Share 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1/2 Series | 198,226 | 214,175 | +8.0% | 9.9% |
| 3/4 Series | 519,228 | 477,180 | −8.1% | 22.0% |
| **5/6 Series** | 250,674 | **299,582** | **+19.5%** | 13.8% |
| **7/8 Series** | 56,542 | **53,399** | **−5.6%** | 2.5% |
| Z4 | 10,482 | 9,744 | −7.0% | 0.4% |
| X1/X2 | 413,386 | 436,769 | +5.7% | 20.1% |
| X3/X4 | 370,198 | 321,186 | −13.2% | 14.8% |
| X5/X6 | 275,318 | 256,941 | −6.7% | 11.8% |
| X7 | 59,949 | 58,089 | −3.1% | 2.7% |
| iX | 38,365 | 35,055 | −8.6% | 1.6% |
| XM | 7,813 | 7,608 | −2.6% | 0.4% |
| **BMW total** | 2,200,217 | 2,169,739 | −1.4% | 100% |

- **X family vs. sedans** (sums of the rows above):

  | | 2025 | Share | Change vs 2024 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | X models (X1/X2, X3/X4, X5/X6, X7, iX, XM) | 1,115,648 | 51.4% | −4.2% |
  | Sedans/coupés (1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, Z4) | 1,054,080 | 48.6% | +1.8% |

  - **Caveat:** these sums are our calculation, not BMW's, and the pairs mix body styles (e.g. 2 Series Active Tourer, 4 Series Gran Coupé).
- **Model highlights:**
  - The 5 Series (with the X2) achieved "strong growth rates" (p. 78).
  - The 7/8 pair is the only premium sedan line declining (−5.6%).
  - Almost one in ten BMWs delivered was an M model (p. 79).

### 1.4 Electrification / EV adoption

| Metric | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Group BEV share of deliveries | 4.1% | 9.0% | 14.7% | 17.4% | **17.9%** | 9 |
| Group electrified (BEV+PHEV) share | 13.0% | 18.1% | 22.2% | 24.2% | **26.1%** | 12 |
| Group BEV units | 103,854 | 215,752 | 375,716 | 426,536 | 442,059 (+3.6%) | 12 |

- **Group PHEV:** 200,012 (+20.0%), share 8.1%. Electrified total 642,071 (+8.2%) (p. 77).
- **BMW brand:** BEV 335,528 (**−8.9%**, 15.5% of the brand); PHEV 199,883 (**+21.8%**, 9.2%) (p. 79). BEV growth came from MINI (105,529 BEV, +87.9%, 36.6% of MINI; p. 80). **PHEV is BMW's growing electrified powertrain.**
- **Model-level adoption:**
  - iX1 was the BMW brand's most successful BEV; >25% of X1 deliveries were BEV.
  - Almost half of 4 Series (Gran Coupé) deliveries were the i4.
  - iX3 (NK) preorders "extend well into 2026" (p. 78).
- **Production:** electrified 597,309 (−8.2%), of which BEV 391,693 (−18.7%) (p. 61).
- **Targets and outlook:**
  - Strategic target: **>50% BEV share of deliveries by 2030**, "albeit with regional differences" (p. 3, 46).
  - 2026 outlook: BEV share "in line with last year's level" (p. 263).
  - Markets are "highly fragmented … demand, especially for electric vehicles, also depends on regional factors": charging infrastructure, cost benefits, energy prices (p. 44).

### 1.5 2026 outlook (as of Mar 2026, p. 263–264)
- **Deliveries:** Group deliveries on a par with 2025. Growth potential in Europe and the USA.
- **China:**
  - BMW "can reach the prior year's level" by stabilising transaction prices.
  - But the market is expected *below* 2025: EV subsidy cuts (especially ≤ CNY 150k) and price regulation (SAMR, Feb 2026).
  - Reality check: actual H1 2026 China was −20.4% (`portfolio-reference.md` §3.5), so the outlook was optimistic.
- **USA:** BEV sales expected to go **down** due to regulatory changes.
- **Europe:** expected to provide most of the market growth (CO₂ rules, subsidies for electrified vehicles).
- **Spending:** R&D expenditure, capex and costs "will be reduced further" in 2026 (p. 264).

### 1.6 Target persona & market prioritization — what the report does and doesn't give
- **It does:**
  - Market weights (§1.2 share of sales).
  - Powertrain trend per brand (§1.4).
  - Model-series momentum (§1.3).
  - BMW's view of customer trends (p. 42):
    - customers shape vehicle requirements around "the digital ecosystems they use daily";
    - "software updates and upgrades have become standard";
    - automated driving is "one of the key expectation[s]", with regional differences in speed;
    - vehicle ownership depends on income, household size and location.
- **It doesn't:** **no demographic/persona data, no per-model regional split, no customer-satisfaction scores** (p. 188–189 describe the survey *processes* only).

---

## 2. Product strategy & R&D

### 2.1 R&D investment priorities

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| R&D expenditure | €9,078 m | **€8,319 m** (−8.4%) | 70, 71, 81 |
| R&D expenditure ratio (% of revenues) | 6.4% | 6.2% | 10, 71 |
| Capitalisation rate | 38.8% | 41.2% | 71 |

- **Focus:** R&D is "related primarily to the **cross-series digitalisation and electrification** of the vehicle fleet". It includes development of **NEUE KLASSE models such as the BMW iX3 and the successors to the BMW X5 and the BMW 7 Series** (p. 70, 81).
- **2026:** R&D expenditure "will be reduced further" (p. 264).
- **Strategic focus areas:**
  1. Technology-open drivetrains with a strong electromobility focus.
  2. Digitalisation of customer interfaces and related products/services.
  3. Sustainability / circular economy (p. 44).
- **Quality programme** "Q3 – Passion for Perfection": quality and reliability are named key factors for customer satisfaction (p. 45).
- **Partners:**
  - Momenta (China ADAS).
  - Qualcomm (automated driving, launching 2026 with the iX3, "subsequently … rolled out across the entire BMW model range"; ~1,300 specialists).
  - Valeo (automated parking) (p. 47, 54, 58).

### 2.2 NEUE KLASSE platform strategy
- **Roll-out:**
  - The NK "technology toolkit and the new design language will be rolled out across the **entire vehicle portfolio, encompassing all drivetrain types, by the end of the decade**" (p. 46).
  - "By 2027, **40 new and revised models** featuring NEUE KLASSE technologies and the new design language" (p. 53).
- **Architecture:**
  - The first NK model (iX3, built in Debrecen) is based on the **"new cluster architecture (NCAR)", focused entirely on BEVs** (p. 46). This is BMW's own platform name; trade press uses others (`portfolio-reference.md` §1).
  - The aim is to "gradually transfer the new vehicle architecture to the global production network over the next years" (p. 59).
- **Model timing:** second NK model i3: Munich, 2026 (p. 53, 59). Munich goes 100% electric by 2027 (p. 47). Spartanburg: ≥6 all-electric X models by 2030 (p. 59).
- **Gen6 eDrive vs. the fifth generation:**
  - Range +30% (iX3 up to **805 km WLTP**).
  - Charging speed +30%.
  - Cylindrical cells with +20% volumetric energy density (p. 54).
  - Gen6 battery assembly: Debrecen (2025), then Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Woodruff/Spartanburg, San Luis Potosí, Shenyang (p. 47, 59).
- **Customer-facing NK technologies:**
  - **BMW Panoramic iDrive:** Panoramic Vision across the full windscreen width, optional 3D head-up display, 17.9″ central display (p. 53).
  - **BMW Operating System X:** in-house, AOSP-based; "high degree of personalisation, regular over-the-air updates and seamless integration of the My BMW app" (p. 53).
  - **BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant with LLM technology:** proactive, personalised routines (p. 53). Alexa Custom Assistant-based since 2024, retrofittable via Remote Software Upgrade (p. 58); Alexa+ (p. 29).
  - **Heart of Joy:** driving-dynamics control unit; "enhances the driving experience" plus efficiency/range (p. 46).
  - **Zonal E/E architecture, "software-defined vehicle"** (p. 54).
  - **Highway & City Assistant:** up to 130 km/h on selected highways; stops at red lights and pulls away in Germany. First UN R171 (DCAS) approval in Germany. **Symbiotic Drive:** steering + braking input without switching the assistant off (p. 54).
  - **Bidirectional charging** on the iX3: V2H, V2G (E.ON offer from Feb 2026), V2L (p. 56).
- **NK in China** ("in China, for China and with China"; p. 28–29, 53–54):
  - iX3 Long Wheelbase: premiere Auto China, April 2026; market entry H2 2026.
  - OS X China has ~70% locally developed software.
  - Amap navigation.
  - LLMs from Alibaba and DeepSeek.
  - Huawei Digital Key, HiCar, and the **My BMW App based on HarmonyOS NEXT**.
  - Momenta L2+ "all scenarios" ADAS tailored to Chinese roads and "user expectations".
  - Media feedback on the iX3 China version: "digital features proving particularly popular" (p. 28).
- **Other drivetrains:**
  - The X5 (presented 2026) will offer five drivetrains: BEV, PHEV, petrol, diesel, hydrogen from 2028. iX5 Hydrogen in 2028 (p. 28, 46, 56).
  - Combustion engines continue alongside BEVs (p. 42, 46).
  - 16 BEV models on offer by end of 2025. iX up to 701 km WLTP; i4 facelift up to 613 km WLTP (p. 46).

### 2.3 ConnectedDrive & My BMW App
- **What the report says (qualitative only):**
  - **Remote Software Upgrade** delivers new features in "infotainment, driver assistance, comfort and safety". Availability depends on "country, model, equipment and software version" (p. 53).

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** "Only about 5% of BMW's sales in China are fully electric … in a market where EVs account for 46%" (Reuters, 14 Jul 2026, Global Mobility data) [S54]. Caveat: the 5% is BEV-only, while the 46% most likely counts BEV+PHEV (NEV), so the gap is overstated. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**Status: proposed (agent-written).** These rules feed a blocking gate (D-008), so a PM must review and sign them off before use. Items marked (PM judgement) are opinions, not evidence.

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

| **EU** | BEV rising, hybrids dominant | EU-27 only (not EFTA/UK) 2025: BEV 17.4% (from 13.6%), PHEV 9.4%, HEV 34.5%, petrol+diesel 35.5% (from 45.2%) | [S40] |

| **US** | BEV fell after the federal credit ended (30 Sep 2025) | BEV peaked at 12% in Sep 2025, then under 6% per month. HEV+BEV+PHEV about 22% in 2025. Q3 2026 forecast: about 6% EV | [S44][S45] |

| CN | German brands declining | Mercedes CN 551,900 (−19%; another source: 472,799 **(conflict)**), BMW −12.5%, Audi 617k (−5.6%), Porsche −26% | [S1][S53][S49][S35] |

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** "Only about 5% of BMW's sales in China are fully electric … in a market where EVs account for 46%" (Reuters, 14 Jul 2026, Global Mobility data) [S54]. Caveat: the 5% is BEV-only, while the 46% most likely counts BEV+PHEV (NEV), so the gap is overstated. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**Status: proposed (agent-written).** These rules feed a blocking gate (D-008), so a PM must review and sign them off before use. Items marked (PM judgement) are opinions, not evidence.

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** "Only about 5% of BMW's sales in China are fully electric … in a market where EVs account for 46%" (Reuters, 14 Jul 2026, Global Mobility data) [S54]. Caveat: the 5% is BEV-only, while the 46% most likely counts BEV+PHEV (NEV), so the gap is overstated. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**Status: proposed (agent-written).** These rules feed a blocking gate (D-008), so a PM must review and sign them off before use. Items marked (PM judgement) are opinions, not evidence.

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

## 1. Platforms

BMW rarely names its platforms in official press releases. Most platform-to-model mappings below therefore rest on trade press. Plant assignments rest on BMW sources.

### 1.1 Current architectures and models

| Architecture | Drive layout / role | Current BMW/MINI models (codes) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CLAR** (Cluster Architecture) | RWD/AWD, multi-energy (ICE/PHEV/BEV) | 3 Series G20/G21 (incl. M3 G80/G81), China LWB 3 Series G28 (incl. China-only BEV i3), 4 Series G22/G23/G26 + i4, 5 Series G60 / Touring G61 / China LWB G68 (incl. i5), 7 Series G70 + i7, 8 Series G14/15/16, X3 G45, China LWB X3, X4 G02 (ended Nov 2025), X5 G05, China LWB X5 G18, X6 G06, X7 G07, XM G09, Z4 G29 (ended 2026), 2 Series Coupé G42 / M2 G87, iX I20 (derivative) | [Trade] S20, S21. Codes are widely used but BMW press does not label them as "CLAR" |
| **FAAR** (successor to UKL2) | FWD/AWD, multi-energy | 1 Series F70, 2 Series Gran Coupé F74, 2 Series Active Tourer U06, X1 U11 + iX1, X2 U10 + iX2, China LWB X1/iX1, MINI Countryman U25 (ICE + BEV) | [Trade] S22, S23. **Conflict:** Wikipedia describes F70 as "UKL2", while bmwblog and others call it FAAR (an evolution of UKL). CnEVPost (S19) calls the China iX1 "CLAR", which is almost certainly wrong |
| MINI legacy UKL | FWD ICE | MINI Cooper 3-door F66, 5-door F65, Convertible F67 (Oxford) | [Unverified] codes; Oxford assignment [BMW] S16 |
| MINI / Great Wall "Spotlight" BEV | FWD BEV | MINI Cooper E/SE J01, Aceman J05 (Zhangjiagang, China; 50:50 JV with Great Wall) | [Trade] S12 |
| **Neue Klasse (NK)** — BMW's own name for the iX3 base: "new cluster architecture (NCAR)", BEV-only [BMW] AR25 p. 46 | Gen6 eDrive, 800 V, cylindrical cells, "superbrain" E/E architecture. BEV-first, but the 8th-gen 3 Series also brings NK design and tech to ICE derivatives | iX3 NA5 (since Oct 2025), i3 sedan NA0 (since Aug 2026); planned: iX3 LWB NA6 (China), i3 Touring NA1, iX4 NA7, i4 Coupé/Convertible NA2/NA3, i7 successor ND0, i1 NB0 (rumoured), NK electric X1 NB5/NB6, NK M cars (ZA0 M3, etc.) | NA5/NA0 and plants [BMW] S7, S9, S10. Codes and future list [Trade] S21 (bmwblog, 12 Dec 2025) |

### 1.2 What NK replaces, and when

- BMW says NK technology goes into **"40 new models and model updates" by 2027** [BMW] S7 (17 Sep 2025). BMW's design chief says every model will get NK design/tech [Trade] S24.
- **NK does not fully replace CLAR before roughly 2030.** The next large SUVs stay on an upgraded CLAR: X5/iX5 G65, X6/iX6 G66, X7/iX7 G67. CLAR is expected "well into the second half of the decade" [Trade] S21 (Dec 2025). **Conflict:** BMW's report lists R&D for "NEUE KLASSE models such as the BMW iX3 and the successors to the BMW X5 and the BMW 7 Series" [BMW] AR25 p. 70, 81. The X5 and G70 successors may be NK-*branded* on a CLAR-derived base (unresolved); Autocar on the next X7 [Trade] S24.
- **Mid-size BEVs move to NK first.** iX3 NA5 replaces the old CLAR iX3 G08. G08 production in China ended in March 2025 [Trade] S19. i3 NA0 replaces the CLAR electric 3 Series/i4 sedan role [Trade] S21.
- **New 3 Series (8th generation, revealed Sep 2026).** The BEV i3 is built in Munich. ICE/PHEV variants are built in Dingolfing, starting with the 320 and M350 petrol models [BMW] S11 (30 Sep 2026). Whether the ICE 3 Series sits on NK hardware or on a CLAR evolution is **[Unverified]**. BMW says the 8th-gen 3 Series "introduces Neue Klasse design and technologies".
- **China.** The China-built CLAR/FAAR BEVs (i3 LWB, i5, iX1) were reported to end production in **July 2026**. The NK iX3 LWB takes over, followed by an NK i3 LWB in early 2027 [Trade] S19 (CnEVPost, 17 Jun 2026, citing "BMW Club"). This is **[Unverified – rumour]**: the sources are a WeChat/Weibo insider relayed by CnEVPost and electrive (18 Jun 2026). BMW has not confirmed it; it only says Shenyang is "laying a solid foundation for the local production of Neue Klasse models". No later report confirms the end of production (checked 2026-10-10). The i7 was imported to China and discontinued there in June 2026 [Trade] S19.
- **FAAR replacement:** no official date. Trade press expects an NK-based electric X1 (NB5/NB6) after the current iX1 cycle, and an i1 (NB0) "toward end of decade" **[Unverified]** S21.

### 1.3 NK rollout timeline

| iX3 LWB (NA6) | Shenyang (BBA, CN) | Pre-series since Dec 2025. BMW says only "2026" for series production. Trade press reports SOP of 50L in Jun 2026 and launch in Q4 2026 (sources conflict). Investment ~CNY 10 bn (~EUR 1.2 bn) | [Trade] S25 (electrive, 5 Jan 2026), S19 |
| i3 sedan (NA0) | Munich (DE) | Pre-series 4 Feb 2026. Orders opened mid-Jun 2026. **SOP Aug 2026** (release dated 6 Aug 2026 says "in August"). Munich builds **BEV only from 2027** | [BMW] S10 (4 Feb 2026), S9 (6 Aug 2026) |
| 3 Series ICE/PHEV (8th gen) | Dingolfing (DE) | Revealed Sep 2026. SOP date not stated | [BMW] S11 |

| China-specific 3 Series | Shenyang | Planned, no date | [BMW] S11 |
| i3 LWB (China) | Shenyang | "Early 2027" | [Trade] S19 |
| iX5 G65 (CLAR, not NK) | Spartanburg (US) | X5 G65 SOP Aug 2026. BMW says iX5 is the first US-built BEV "before year end" 2026. Other reports say early or late 2027 (conflict). At least 6 BEVs built in the US by 2030 | [BMW] via S27; [Trade] S27, S28 |

Gen6 supply chain: Debrecen is the first of five Gen6 battery plants [BMW] S7. Irlbach-Straßkirchen (DE) starts operating in Oct 2026, has 2 lines and makes up to 1,000 batteries per day for all German plants [BMW] S9, S13. E-motors come from Steyr (AT) [BMW] S9. Woodruff, SC supplies Spartanburg [Trade] S27.

- **Mid-size BEVs move to NK first.** iX3 NA5 replaces the old CLAR iX3 G08. G08 production in China ended in March 2025 [Trade] S19. i3 NA0 replaces the CLAR electric 3 Series/i4 sedan role [Trade] S21.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:

The most recent figures are for 2025. The M2 is the strongest manual seller, and the M3/M4 numbers depend on how you count buyers.

- **M2:** The manual take rate fell from about 50% in 2024 to about 40% in 2025, according to BMW USA The M2 with a manual is also less popular than it was in 2024. According to BMW USA, the take rate has fallen from 50% to 40%.
- **M3 and M4, all buyers:** Counting every trim, roughly 6 to 10% of M3 and M4 buyers chose the manual in 2025. That total includes the automatic-only Competition, Competition xDrive, and M4 Convertible Competition xDrive around 6 to 10 percent of total M3 and M4 buyers opted for the manual. But those figures take into account automatic-only models.
- **M3 and M4, manual-eligible trims only:** Limited to the rear-wheel-drive base models that offer a manual, nearly a third of M4 buyers—around 33 percent—opted for the manual, while nearly half of M3 buyers went with the stick. Motor1 notes that those numbers are down slightly across the board compared to 2024.
- **2024 comparison:** Motor1's 2024 figures were M2 at 50%, M3 at 20%, and M4 at 15%, with the same caveat that the manual is available on the A-Spec Technology package applies to other brands. For BMW, the manual was only on base trims, so the all-trim share looked low.

Sources differ on the M3/M4 number because of the denominator. Motor1 and BMWBlog both report the all-trim 6–10% figure and the eligible-trim ~33% (M4) and ~50% (M3) figures for 2025. Some earlier reports (2023 and 2024) gave the M3/M4 rate as 20%, which was a different basis.

- **EU-wide estimate:** A Transport & Environment report says corporate fleets account for six out of ten new car sales. The European Commission's explanatory memo for its fleet decarbonisation proposal puts corporate registrations at around 60% of car registrations in the EU.

The results don't include a clear 2025 survey, but several recent polls report majority or near-majority preference for physical buttons.

- **New Zealand (AutoSense poll, Sept 2026):** Of 476 New Zealanders, 49% rated knobs and buttons as the easiest controls to use while driving, while just 6% picked touchscreens, and one in five wanted both.
- **UK (Startline/APD survey):** Eight out of 10 (79%) motorists say they would rather have buttons for major controls than a big, central touchscreen. The sample was 302 consumers. The results don't show a survey date, so I can't confirm it's from 2025.
- **UK (What Car? survey):** Nearly 90 per cent of UK motorists prefer physical buttons rather than touch-sensitive controls. This survey of 1,428 motorists appears to be from 2024, based on the article's URL.
- **UK (Quotezone survey, May 2026):** A narrower question found that 47% of UK drivers believe touchscreen dashboards make driving more distracting when compared to using physical buttons.
- **Global (S&P Global, 2026):** Preferences are more mixed. Nearly half (48%) of global respondents prefer a combination of touchscreens with physical buttons or knobs.

Overall, the strongest preference for buttons appears in UK surveys, with figures ranging from 79% to nearly 90% depending on the question wording. Globally, hybrid setups get more support than buttons alone.

The search turned up Deloitte's 2026 study details for fuel costs and range concerns, but nothing on premium buyers specifically.

- **Fuel costs:** Among U.S. respondents, lower fuel costs are the top reason (52%) they would consider an EV for their next purchase. A trade publication reporting on the study says this reflects a desire to reduce total cost of ownership.
- **Range and charging:** A summary of the study says lower running costs keep electrified options under consideration, but concerns about limited range, long charging times, patchy public charging, and long-term battery reliability remain prominent.
- **Charging access:** Home charging is still the preferred option for most people considering an EV. Public charging costs also weigh heavily on decisions.

- **Mintel's 2025 China luxury car owners report** says technology is overtaking traditional luxury car badges as the key consumer demand. It surveyed 1,000 internet users aged 18-59 who own luxury cars worth more than RMB300,000.
- **Mintel's 2024 edition** (earlier survey) found that 65% and 37% of surveyed luxury car owners, respectively, value a premium consumer experience and exclusivity when making car purchase decisions. (engine|delivery)|performance)\b",
    "P-DIGI": r"\b(apps?|my bmw|smartphone|carplay|android auto|voice (command|control|assistant|recognition)|assistant|alexa|over[- ]the[- ]air|ota|software update|remote software|digital key|phone as key|wireless charg\w*|streaming|connected ?drive|subscription|head[- ]up display|hud|curved display|augmented|personali[sz]\w*|profile|ai\b|gesture)\b",

}
RX = {k: re.compile(v) for k, v in CUES.items()}

rows = con.execute("""
WITH latest AS (SELECT source_item_id, max(extractor_version) v FROM signal GROUP BY 1)
SELECT si.vehicle_model_id, si.market_code, s.source_item_id, s.category, s.feedback_type,

FROM signal s JOIN latest l ON l.source_item_id=s.source_item_id AND l.v=s.extractor_version
JOIN source_item si ON si.id=s.source_item_id
WHERE si.kind='feedback'
""").fetchall()

sig_tot = defaultdict(int); verb_tot = defaultdict(set)
sig_hit = defaultdict(int); verb_hit = defaultdict(set)
for der, mkt, sid, cat, ft, txt in rows:
    key = (der, mkt)

    for p, rx in RX.items():
        if rx.search(txt):
            sig_hit[key + (p,)] += 1; verb_hit[key + (p,)].add(sid)

out = []
for key in sorted(sig_tot):
    for p in CUES:
        k = key + (p,)
        out.append(dict(derivative=key[0], market=key[1], persona_id=p,
                        signal_hits=sig_hit[k], signals_total=sig_tot[key],
                        verbatim_hits=len(verb_hit[k]), verbatims_total=len(verb_tot[key]),
                        signal_share=round(sig_hit[k]/sig_tot[key], 3)))
json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[2], "w"), indent=1)
# print a compact table
print("der mkt n_sig n_verb | " + " ".join(f"{p[2:]:>11}" for p in CUES))
for key in sorted(sig_tot):
    cells = []
    for p in CUES:
        k = key + (p,)
        cells.append(f"{sig_hit[k]:>5}({sig_hit[k]/sig_tot[key]*100:3.0f}%)")
    print(f"{key[0]} {key[1]:>3} {sig_tot[key]:>5} {len(verb_tot[key]):>5} | " + " ".join(cells))

input.content:
# Customer Segments (Personas) and Model Groups

**Status:** v1, proposed (agent-written research seed, 2026-10-11). The PM must review it before the app uses it. Plan pillar P3 (`plan-v2.md`).
**Data:** `data/seed/personas.json` holds the personas, model groups, weight estimates and data-check counts. It is git-ignored with the rest of `data/`.

## 1. Why

- **The problem.** Today the app treats each derivative × market as one average customer. BMW has several customer groups, and their needs differ:
  - the enthusiast wants raw, mechanical driving feel;
  - the China rear-seat passenger wants a lounge;
  - the tech buyer wants a phone on wheels.
- **What an average hides:**
  - *Conflicts.* Physical buttons vs. bigger screens. Firm sporty chassis vs. floaty chauffeur ride.
  - *Small, loyal groups.* M buyers are about 1 in 10 BMWs, but they carry the brand.
- **What personas add:**
  - who a requirement serves;
  - what each group must not lose;
  - where requirements collide.

## 2. Persona cards

Each persona maps to our requirement categories. Cue examples are paraphrased; full lists are in the JSON.

### P-ENTH — Driving purist / enthusiast
- **Who:** buys a BMW for how it drives: steering, balance, sound and responsive power.
- **Values:**
  - Driving Experience: steering, handling, sport modes.
  - Powertrain (as experienced): power delivery, sound.
  - Interior: sport seats, driver cockpit.
  - Variants & Packages: M / M Sport, manual where offered.
  - Design & Quality Perception: sporty look.
- **Must-not-lose:** steering feel; chassis balance; throttle response; sound character; driver controls (paddles, HUD, physical shortcuts).
- **Deal-breakers:** numb steering or a soft default setup; fake or missing sound; agility lost to weight; assistance that can't be switched off.
- **Typical models:** F70 M135 / M Sport, G60 M5 / M60 / 540i, M2, M3.
- **Evidence:**
  - M is 9.8% of BMW sales, and the US is the largest M market at >72k units (BMW PressClub, 2026-01-09, T1).
  - The M2 manual take rate is about 40%; 6–10% of all M3/M4 buyers chose the manual (Motor1 / bmwblog, 2026-01, T2).
  - F70 EU study: Sportiness z = +1.36 (BMW study, T1).
- **Cue:** praises steering on a twisty road; wants more sound in sport mode; says it feels slower than the previous BMW. *Not:* off-centre wheel after an alignment (defect).

### P-DIGI — Digital-first / tech buyer
- **Who:** judges the car like a smartphone.
- **Values:**
  - Infotainment & Digital: phone-like UI and ecosystem; LLM voice; OTA, digital key and app.
  - Driver Assistance (as experienced): hands-off / navigation-based assistance and parking.
  - Interior: big screens and HUD.
  - Range & Charging: smart charge planning.
- **Must-not-lose:** software that improves after purchase; reliable connectivity; assisted driving on par with local leaders.
- **Deal-breakers:** laggy or buggy infotainment; paywalls for hardware already in the car; launching behind Huawei / Xiaomi in China.
- **Typical models:** G68 and G70 in China, i5, NK iX3 / i3.
- **Evidence:**
  - ADAS is the #1 purchase reason for China premium NEV buyers (Reuters, 2026-07-14, T2).
  - 45% of Chinese luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity (Mintel 2024, T2).
  - Half of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS (McKinsey Pulse 2026, T2).
  - BMW: customers expect "the digital ecosystems they use daily" (BMW Group Report 2025 p. 42, T1).
  - Study: Connected services is the weakest or near-weakest item for every model (z −0.99 to −1.95).
- **Cue:** wants natural voice requests; more apps; hands-free highway; features arriving by update. *Not:* wants a climate button back (that is P-TRAD).

### P-CHAUF — Comfort & chauffeur / rear-seat executive
- **Who:** sits in the back, either chauffeured or hosting parents or business guests.
- **Values:**
  - Comfort & Space: rear legroom, lounge seats, quiet ride, rear climate and massage.
  - Infotainment & Digital: rear entertainment (Theatre Screen, rear controls).
  - Interior: rear materials and sunshades.
  - Variants & Packages: LWB body, executive packages.
- **Must-not-lose:** rear space and comfort; quietness; working rear controls; the LWB body in China.
- **Deal-breakers:**
  - a smaller rear than local LWB rivals at the same price;
  - rear features that cheaper domestic rivals offer and BMW lacks (zero-gravity seat, fridge, screens).
- **Typical models:** G68 5 Series Li, G70 in CN / KR / EU executive use, 3 Series Li.
- **Evidence:**
  - "Chinese buyers value spacious cabins with generous rear-seat legroom"; the "L" naming is a "chauffeur-friendly" positioning (bmwblog, 2026-01-22, T2).
  - The long 5 Series is "one of the absolute bestsellers in China" (bmwblog, 2017, T2).
  - Competitors: E-Class L at 3,094 mm, A6L; AITO M9 and Maextro S800 rear lounges (competitor-landscape §1b–c).
  - Study: G68 CN rear roominess z = +0.81 (a strength); G70 CN rear roominess z = −1.57 (a pain).
- **Cue:** more legroom behind the passenger seat; rear sunshades; rear screen is the highlight. *Not:* tighter driver-seat bolsters.

### P-STAT — Status & design seeker
- **Who:** buys the badge and the look.
- **Values:**
  - Exterior: presence and design (grille, lights, wheels), signature lighting.
  - Design & Quality Perception: perceived quality and materials, prestige that matches the price.
  - Interior: crystal and ambient details.
  - Variants & Packages: Individual colours, top trims.
- **Must-not-lose:** brand prestige; exterior presence; premium cabin materials.
- **Deal-breakers:** a design that reads as cheap or generic; visible cost-cutting; a badge diluted by discounts.
- **Typical models:** G70 in all markets, G68, G60 in the US and RoW.
- **Evidence:**
  - Study: Prestige is a top item for every model (z +0.77 to +1.22).
  - 65% / 37% of Chinese luxury owners value a premium experience / exclusivity (Mintel 2024, T2).
  - The 7 Series won 2024 US APEAL (J.D. Power, T2).
  - BMW's grille strategy is China-driven and polarising (The Drive, T3).
- **Cue:** people compliment the car; interior plastics feel cheap for the price; wants exclusive colours. *Not:* bigger boot.

### P-FAM — Family & practical
- **Who:** uses the car as the household's main vehicle.
- **Values:**
  - Comfort & Space: rear space, child seats, boot and loading.
  - Interior: storage, cupholders, charging points for all rows.
  - Infotainment & Digital: rear entertainment for kids.
  - Driver Assistance (as experienced): parking and safety.
  - Variants & Packages: Touring and LWB bodies.
- **Must-not-lose:** rear space; boot; everyday ease.
- **Deal-breakers:** no room for a pram; awkward child seats; little storage.
- **Typical models:** F70, G60 (Touring not in the provided data), G68; X models.
- **Evidence:**
  - Study: Luggage capacity is a pain for F70 EU (z −2.27), G60 EU (z −1.04) and G70 (z −1.34 / −1.57).
  - Europe 2025 sales: hatchbacks 23.9%, wagons 7.1% (Dataforce, T2).
  - In US G70 data the Theatre Screen is used by children, e.g. a son watching cartoons (G70-0091).
- **Cue:** boot too small for a stroller; easier child-seat fitting. *Not:* trunk lid rattles (defect).

### P-EV — Pragmatic EV switcher / efficiency-minded
- **Who:** goes BEV or PHEV, or simply wants low running costs, for practical reasons.
- **Values:**
  - Range & Charging: real range (winter, highway); fast, reliable charging and home charging.
  - Powertrain (as experienced): efficiency, PHEV electric range for the commute.
  - Infotainment & Digital: accurate range prediction and charge planning.
  - Comfort & Space: preconditioning.
  - Variants & Packages: powertrain choice.
- **Must-not-lose:** a range estimate you can trust; charging that works first time; low running cost.
- **Deal-breakers:** cold or highway range far below the stated figure; broken public charging; no PHEV where chargers are scarce.
- **Typical models:** i5 / 550e, i7 / 750e, i5 LWB, NK iX3 / i3.
- **Evidence:**
  - US: lower fuel costs are the #1 reason to consider an EV (52%); range is the #1 concern (47%) (Deloitte 2026, T2).
  - 89% of EV owners would buy another plug-in (McKinsey 2026, T2).
  - BMW PHEV +21.8% while BEV −8.9% (BMW Group Report 2025, T1).
  - BEV/PHEV share of our verbatims: G60 US 44%, G70 US 36%, G60 EU 75%.
- **Cue:** winter range far below expectation; PHEV range for the commute. *Not:* the wireless phone charger overheats.

### P-BIZ — Company-car / high-mileage business driver
- **Who:** drives many motorway kilometres on a company car or lease.
- **Values:**
  - Driver Assistance (as experienced): adaptive cruise, lane centering, hands-off highway.
  - Comfort & Space: long-distance seats, low motorway noise.
  - Powertrain (as experienced): efficiency and range between stops.
  - Infotainment & Digital: calls and navigation.
  - Range & Charging: motorway fast charging.
  - Variants & Packages: business packages.
- **Must-not-lose:** long-distance comfort; highway assistance that cuts fatigue; range or efficiency.
- **Deal-breakers:** phantom braking or weak highway assistance; a noisy cabin at speed; missing fleet-standard equipment.
- **Typical models:** G60 in the EU (DE / UK), G70 EU executive, F70 EU user-chooser.
- **Evidence:**
  - Corporate fleets are "six out of ten new car sales" in the EU; company cars average 105,000 km per lease (T&E, T2).
  - 3 and 5 Series diesel registrations in Germany are "buoyed by company-car and fleet demand" (bmwblog / KBA, 2026-01, T2).
  - US premium lease penetration is in the low- to mid-40% range (WardsAuto, 2026-02-17, T2).
- **Cue:** adaptive cruise makes motorway trips relaxed; wind noise at highway speed. *Not:* bigger rear screen for kids.

### P-TRAD — Loyal traditionalist
- **Who:** a long-time BMW owner who likes the iDrive knob and tactile buttons and dislikes change for its own sake.
- **Values:**
  - Interior: physical controls.
  - Infotainment & Digital: shallow menus, low distraction.
  - Design & Quality Perception: solid build.
  - Driving Experience: classic BMW character.
  - Comfort & Space: simple climate controls.
  - Variants & Packages: no forced bundles.
- **Must-not-lose:** iDrive controller and physical shortcuts; climate control without menus; consistency with earlier BMWs.
- **Deal-breakers:** touch-only core functions; features removed that they had before.
- **Typical models:** F70 in the EU and UK, G60 and G70 in the US.
- **Evidence:**
  - Euro NCAP 2026 rewards physical controls for core functions (ETSC, T2).
  - 47% of UK drivers find touchscreens more distracting than buttons (Quotezone via Road Safety GB, 2026-05-06, T3).
  - 48% of global respondents want touch + buttons (S&P Global 2026, T2).
  - F70 reviews criticise touch climate and the loss of the iDrive knob (Top Gear / Auto Express, T2).
  - Own data: one F70 owner said losing the iDrive controller "feels like going backwards" (F70-0403).
- **Cue:** misses the rotary controller; wants a heated-seat button instead of a menu. *Not:* wants more apps.

## 3. Persona weights per derivative × market (ESTIMATES)

**Read this first:**
- These are **judgement estimates, not measured shares.**
- Each row sums to 1.
- **Basis:** BMW study z-scores, our feedback (engine mix and data-check cue shares) and the web sources above.
- China has **no verbatims**, so its rows rest on the study and web sources only.
- The basis for each row is in `persona_weights[].basis`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 × EU | .20 | .13 | .00 | .17 | .15 | .12 | .10 | .13 |
| F70 × RoW (JP) | .20 | .12 | .00 | .20 | .15 | .13 | .05 | .15 |
| G60 × EU | .15 | .12 | .03 | .10 | .10 | .15 | **.25** | .10 |

## 4. Data check: are the personas visible in BMW feedback?

**Method:**
- **Input:** a keyword regex per persona over `topic + need_statement + quote` of the `signal` table. Only the latest extractor version per verbatim is used.
- **Multi-label:** one signal can hit several personas.
- **Precision check:** a 10-hit sample per persona was hand-checked. Generic words were removed ("button", "removed"), and phone/USB charging was excluded from P-EV.
- **What the counts mean:** cue *mentions*, not persona sizes.
- **Weakest cues:** P-ENTH also catches neutral "performance" statements, and P-STAT catches generic "design" likes. These are the noisiest.

Signal hits (share of signals in that cell):

| F70 × EU | 3,922 | 681 (17%) | 147 (4%) | 37 (1%) | 378 (10%) | 115 (3%) | 260 (7%) | 52 (1%) | 169 (4%) |
| F70 × RoW | 1,452 | 304 (21%) | 32 (2%) | 3 (0%) | 117 (8%) | 26 (2%) | 138 (10%) | 45 (3%) | 17 (1%) |
| G60 × EU | 314 | 36 (11%) | 18 (6%) | 0 | 24 (8%) | 13 (4%) | 56 (18%) | 9 (3%) | 8 (3%) |
| G60 × US | 4,757 | 556 (12%) | 411 (9%) | 57 (1%) | 524 (11%) | 213 (4%) | 484 (10%) | 163 (3%) | 152 (3%) |
| G60 × RoW | 507 | 101 (20%) | 11 (2%) | 4 (1%) | 69 (14%) | 11 (2%) | 54 (11%) | 12 (2%) | 10 (2%) |
| G70 × EU | 50 | 7 | 1 | 0 | 5 | 3 | 5 | 1 | 2 |

**Takeaways:**
- **Enthusiast:** strong everywhere. Highest in F70 RoW (21%), G60 RoW (20%) and F70 EU (17%).
- **Status / design:** visible everywhere, highest in the 7 Series (13–15%).
- **Digital:** only visible in the US (8–9%). It is likely under-counted, because China, its main market, has no verbatims.
- **EV:** strongest where BEV/PHEV verbatims dominate (G60 EU 18%).
- **Chauffeur:** nearly invisible (≤3%). The data has no CN verbatims, and the US G70 rear-screen talk is often about kids. This persona rests on the study and web sources: **that is an evidence gap, not proof of absence.**
- **Business driver:** low as a keyword signal (1–4%). EU G60 / G70 data is thin.
- **Traditionalist:** 3–4% in F70 EU and the US. That is a small share, but it ties directly to the F70 control-layout critique.

## 5. Model groups

   - **EV vs. ENTH:** efficiency and weight vs. sound and power. Synthetic sound and NK Heart of Joy are a possible bridge.
   - **DIGI (CN) vs. global platform:** China-only digital stack vs. a global OS.
5. **Views:** priorities per persona; persona mix per derivative × market; model-group view for platform-wide requirements (portfolio-leverage factor).

- **China blind spot.** No verbatims exist. CN weights come from the study and from web sources, mostly T2.
- **US bias.** G60 and G70 feedback is 90–95% US, so US personas dominate any data-driven count.
- **Keyword counts are rough.** They measure cue frequency, not people. They over-count generic "design/performance" likes and under-count implicit needs.
- **Overlap.** One customer can be several personas (a chauffeur buyer is often status-driven). Tags are multi-label.
- **Sources:**
  - Some quotes are paraphrases of existing knowledge-base entries; the JSON marks these "(paraphrase)".
  - The S&P Global page returned 403. Its figure comes from the search summary.
  - The Mintel figures come from report abstracts.
- **Scope.** Personas describe customer-facing needs only. "Company car" here means usage patterns, not pricing or tax.
